powertrains: ICE (48V mild hybrid: E 350 2.0T, E 450 3.0T I6)
rationale: Mercedes' core mid-size luxury sedan and the most direct US rival of the BMW 5 Series (G60). MBUSA lists the MY2027 sedan as E 350 from $65,200, E 450 4MATIC $73,700 and AMG E 53 Hybrid $91,100, a line-up that mirrors 530i/540i/550e. US press pits the E450 directly against the 540i (Autoblog comparison, Car and Driver 540i test) and KBB runs a 5 Series vs E-Class comparison. BMW's own G60 US feedback mentions Mercedes about 30 times.
next_generation: Comprehensive facelift of the combustion/PHEV W214 reported for 2027, adopting the design language of the coming electric E-Class (see us_mercedes-O001).

announcement: Comprehensive facelift of the combustion/PHEV E-Class reported for 2027, launching alongside the new electric (seventh-generation) E-Class.
customer_facing_changes: Exterior design adopts the design language of the new electric E-Class
Combustion and PHEV versions continue in sedan and estate form on the MRA II platform

statement: Owner of a 2025 E 350 rates the build quality as excellent.
Owner states the four-cylinder E 350 has sufficient power and runs at only about 1,300 rpm at 65 mph.
Owner states the cabin is quiet at highway speed.
Owner reports about 42 mpg on the highway with two people aboard and cruise control set at 65 mph.
Owner states the air vents give very good airflow without blowing directly on the occupants.
Owner finds the voice command system helpful.
Owner states the voice assistant sometimes activates unexpectedly.
Owner states rear foot room is too tight, making a one-hour trip in the back uncomfortable; a 2024 Toyota Camry's rear seat felt more comfortable.
Owner finds getting in and out of the car difficult, even after adjusting the seat.
Owner misses a front seat thigh extension for tall drivers and passengers.
Owner reports the adaptive cruise control braked hard without warning on the highway, dropping from 65 to 35 mph, most often near exits.
Owner states lane departure warning gives only a faint steering-wheel vibration and does not steer the car back, unlike the family's Toyota, Hyundai and VW cars.
Owner complains there is no spare tire; with run-flat tires, a flat after hours or on a weekend meant waiting about two days for a replacement.
Owner states the touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls change the instrument cluster display too easily.
Owner reports the right windshield wiper makes a loud noise in light rain, and a friend's car has the same issue.
Owner finds the standard speakers adequate, although louder audio would need the roughly $1,000 Burmester 4D option.
Owner questions spending about $72,000 on the car and says they would not make the same purchase again.
Owner states the car rides comfortably and is easy to handle.

statement: Owner states the car almost drives itself thanks to its many electronics.
Owner says this is their fifth E-Class and all previous ones were reliable and safe.

Reviewer states the E450 rides smoothly and the optional Airmatic air suspension gives a serene ride, one reason to pick it over the 540i.
Reviewer praises the E450's 375-hp mild-hybrid inline-six and rates it on par with the 540i (both 0-60 mph in 4.4 s), though the BMW has more torque.
Reviewer states the E450's 9-speed automatic could be quicker to downshift.
Reviewer notes the E450 is rated 25 mpg combined versus 28 mpg for the 540i.
Reviewer rates the E-Class interior as more visually striking and of better material quality than the 5 Series.
Reviewer credits the E-Class with an optional front-passenger display next to its 14.4-inch touchscreen.
Reviewer credits the BMW with keeping a physical rotary controller, which the touchscreen-based E-Class lacks.
Reviewer notes the E-Class trunk is much smaller than the 540i's (12.7 vs 18.4 cu ft).
Reviewer describes both the E450 and the 540i as spacious for front and rear passengers.
Reviewer finds the E-Class classier and more sophisticated looking, while calling the BMW's grille oddly large and its exterior hard to love.
Reviewer notes the E-Class can be too easily confused with the C-Class or S-Class.
Reviewer states the optional rear-wheel steering makes the E450 feel smaller than its dimensions suggest.
Reviewer notes a surround-view camera is standard on the E450 but optional on the 540i.
Reviewer notes the E450 starts at $73,700 versus $67,700 for the 540i, and many standalone options and packages push its price higher still.
Reviewer would buy the pricier E450 over the 540i because it feels like the more special luxury car.
quote: feels like the more special luxury car

statement: Reviewer states the 540i felt a size too big next to the E450 and its smaller glass area makes the BMW cabin feel more confining.
Reviewer states both cars ride supplely, but the E450's optional adaptive dampers can be set softer, which suits rough Michigan roads better.
Reviewer states the 540i feels heavier than the Mercedes (it weighs 101 lb more) and its steering is light on effort and feedback.
Reviewer notes the base E 350 is rated 25/33/28 mpg (city/highway/combined) versus 28/35/31 mpg for the 530i.

vfc_level2: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology
statement: Reviewer judges both sedans refined and poised and calls the choice of driving feel a matter of taste.
Reviewer favours the E-Class for buyers who want the newest tech, citing the Superscreen, Burmester 4D audio and an optional AI that learns routines.
KBB's spec comparison shows the E-Class with less rear headroom (37.6 vs 39.1 in) and rear legroom (36.2 vs 37.0 in) than the 5 Series.
Reviewer notes every E-Class variant gains a center airbag.
Reviewer lists a KBB Fair Purchase Price of $58,000 for the E 350 versus $54,700 for the 530i, while calling overall pricing similar.
Reviewer notes the E-Class powertrain warranty (4 years/50,000 miles) is shorter than the 5 Series' 6 years/70,000 miles.
Reviewer finds the E350's 255-hp 2.0-liter mild-hybrid powertrain silky and adequately powerful for the car's purpose.
Reviewer states the optional adaptive air suspension soaks up potholes and expansion joints without losing body control.
Reviewer finds the brakes touchy, sometimes causing a sudden lurch that surprised passengers.
Reviewer praises the optional Superscreen's graphics, processing speed and animations; the passenger screen streams video and goes private while driving.
Reviewer praises the cabin's gloss-black, frosted-aluminum and dark-wood trim and the rich optional leather.
Reviewer suspects the screen-heavy cockpit, aimed at younger buyers, may not appeal to traditional Mercedes buyers.
Reviewer warns that options and packages add up quickly; the loaded test car reached $82,000 against a $63,450 base price.

rationale: Mercedes' electric mid-size luxury sedan and the direct US rival of the BMW i5 (G60 BEV). KBB's 2025 EQE review benchmarks it against the i5 eDrive40 (range 308 vs 295 mi, trunk 11 vs 17.3 cu ft, similar ~30 min 10-80 % charging); Canadian comparison tests (AutoTrader.ca, Auto123) pit the AMG EQE against the i5 M60. MBUSA still lists a 2026 EQE sedan (EQE 320+, 96 kWh, 308 mi). BMW's own G60 US feedback mentions Mercedes about 30 times.
next_generation: Electric E-Class ('E-Class with EQ Technology', MB.EA platform, three-box sedan) reported to replace the EQE from 2027 (see us_mercedes-O002).

announcement: Seventh-generation electric E-Class reported to debut in 2027 and replace the EQE sedan.
customer_facing_changes: Traditional three-box sedan silhouette with a long, status-oriented wheelbase instead of the EQE's one-bow shape (reported)
MB.EA platform shared with the GLC EQ and electric C-Class (reported)
800 V architecture with up to 350 kW DC charging (expected)
Single-motor RWD and dual-motor AWD versions, adaptive air suspension and rear-wheel steering (expected)
EQ naming dropped and EVs styled like combustion models (Mercedes statement)

Reviewer states the narrow rear window limits the view behind and the tall dashboard hurts forward visibility.

Reviewer notes the i5's trunk holds 60 litres more, although the EQE's rear seatbacks fold electrically.
Reviewer reports negative feedback on the EQE's styling, with one editor saying it looked like it was melting; the i5's styling is preferred.
Reviewer notes the AMG EQE uses more energy (3.2 vs 2.6 Le/100 km) and has less rated range (362 vs 399 km) than the i5 M60.
Reviewer notes the AMG EQE's 170 kW peak DC charging rate trails the i5's 205 kW.
Reviewer calls the i5's value advantage dramatic: the AMG EQE starts at C$121,500 versus C$95,000 for the i5 M60.
Reviewer scores the AMG EQE and i5 M60 equally (9/10) on safety.
Reviewer calls the powertrain contest between the AMG EQE and i5 M60 a tie, although the AMG is quicker on paper (0-100 km/h 3.3 vs 3.7 s).
Reviewer states the EQE's adaptive suspension stays supple and gentle, while the i5 transmits more road unevenness even in Comfort mode.
Reviewer finds the EQE's steering a little heavy, while the i5 feels lighter and more agile in tight urban spaces.
Reviewer rates the EQE's interior better than the i5's, praising its luxurious ambience and finish.
Reviewer finds BMW's infotainment system easier to use than MBUX.
Reviewer states voice control works very well in both the EQE and the i5.
Reviewer prefers the i5's sportier look and finds the EQE's styling too conservative.
Reviewer notes the EQE needs 32 minutes for 10-80 % at up to 170 kW, versus 20-30 minutes at up to 205 kW for the i5.
Reviewer lists the EQE's on-board space as a strength and says the i5 has a smaller interior.
Reviewer notes the AMG EQE starts at C$121,000 versus C$97,500 for the i5 M60, which rivals or beats it on almost every criterion.
Reviewer praises a smooth, calm ride with a quiet electric powertrain.
Reviewer states the low center of gravity gives agility and optional rear-wheel steering adds highway stability and a tight turning circle.
Reviewer calls the EQE 350 4MATIC's roughly 6-second 0-60 mph time not brilliant and notes the i5 eDrive40 is 0.3 s quicker.
Reviewer notes the EQE 350+ is rated at 308 miles of range versus 295 miles for the base i5 eDrive40.
Reviewer lists as a con that the EQE 350 4MATIC and 500 4MATIC dropped to 267 miles of range, from 298.
Reviewer states 10-80 % DC fast charging takes about 30 minutes, similar to the BMW i5.
Reviewer describes the cabin as high-tech and luxurious, with comfortable seats and high-quality materials.
Reviewer states the EQE's rear seat is roomier than the E-Class's, with no transmission tunnel.
Reviewer notes the swooping roofline means bending more to get into the car.
Reviewer calls the 11-cu-ft trunk small; the i5 offers 17.3 cu ft.
Reviewer praises the full-width Hyperscreen and calls the EQE's tech superb.
Reviewer notes KBB Fair Purchase Prices run about $4,850-5,550 below MSRP and expects above-average resale values.
